title: The Months: Gods and Beginnings
label: ch:months-gods
canDo: I can name the first six months in French and say which Roman figure each one carries.

payoff.summary: Six months, and not one of them is a number. The calendar is a procession of Roman gods and festivals carried almost unchanged out of Latin -- Janus in the doorway of the year, the Februa that cleaned the city before it turned, and the war-god who already owns a weekday.
payoff.note: Authored as part of the chapter-9 split: length is never a cost, so sixteen months-and-seasons became three chapters rather than one dense one. The payoff is atom-scored -- it assesses every atom its chapter introduces.
